Definition: Whether the instant payment system supports business payments to suppliers, vendors, contractors, and other businesses for commercial transactions, procurement, and supply chain payments.
Comments: Mobile money in Benin is used for “business transactions” and other uses (loan repayment, savings), supporting the existence of digital channels that businesses can use to pay other businesses/suppliers (B2B) ([IMF eLibrary – Benin Digital Transformation to Foster Inclusive Growth](https://www.elibrary.imf.org/view/journals/002/2024/339/article-A002-en.xml)). Also, PI‑SPI supports instant payments and transfers between participating institutions (banks and mobile money), which can be used by businesses where offered ([BCEAO press release – PI‑SPI participants at launch](https://www.bceao.int/fr/communique-presse/liste-des-participants-autorises-ouvrir-les-services-de-pi-spi-au-public-30-sept-2025)).

Definition: Whether the instant payment system is used or can be used for government disbursements to citizens, including social transfers, welfare payments, salaries, pensions, subsidies, grants, and emergency assistance.
Comments: World Bank Implementation Status & Results Report for the Benin Economic Governance for Service Delivery Program-for-Results reports a 31-Dec-2023 indicator where “0 percent of beneficiaries of the social programs receive digital G2P payments,” implying G2P digitization was not yet in active use for those programs at that time ([World Bank ISR – Benin Economic Governance for Service Delivery PforR](https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/099092325063510323/pdf/P176763-2035557c-fe0f-4162-a072-04b417dfb137.pdf)). Given evidence indicates no G2P digitization for social program beneficiaries (at least through 2023), score as No.

Definition: Whether the system enables consumer payments to merchants and businesses for goods and services, including retail purchases, bill payments, e-commerce, and subscription services.
Comments: Mobile money in Benin is used for “payment of bills and services” and “business transactions,” indicating P2B merchant/service payments via mobile money ([IMF eLibrary – Benin Digital Transformation to Foster Inclusive Growth](https://www.elibrary.imf.org/view/journals/002/2024/339/article-A002-en.xml)). PI‑SPI supports interoperable “payments” as part of instant operations across participating institutions ([BCEAO press release – PI‑SPI participants at launch](https://www.bceao.int/fr/communique-presse/liste-des-participants-autorises-ouvrir-les-services-de-pi-spi-au-public-30-sept-2025)).

Definition: Whether the instant payment system supports direct person-to-person transfer of funds between individuals for informal transactions, remittances, and interpersonal value transfers.
Comments: Mobile money is widely used in Benin for money transfers/remittances and other transactions (P2P included) per IMF discussion of mobile money usage ([IMF eLibrary – Benin Digital Transformation to Foster Inclusive Growth](https://www.elibrary.imf.org/view/journals/002/2024/339/article-A002-en.xml)). PI‑SPI also supports instant interoperable “fund transfers and payments” across account types in WAEMU including Benin ([BCEAO press release – PI‑SPI participants at launch](https://www.bceao.int/fr/communique-presse/liste-des-participants-autorises-ouvrir-les-services-de-pi-spi-au-public-30-sept-2025)).

Definition: Whether and how the central bank participates in payment system governance beyond its regulatory oversight role, including board representation, operational management, technical standard-setting, or direct system operation.
Comments: BCEAO states it is “responsible for the management” (operational + technical) of SICA‑UEMOA and STAR‑UEMOA under Article 3 of Regulation No. 15/2002/CM/WAMU, including transaction supervision, incident handling, reporting, and settlement risk tools (Guarantee Fund, intraday advances) ([BCEAO – Payment Systems Management](https://www.bceao.int/en/content/payment-systems-management)). PI‑SPI ownership/operator is also indicated as BCEAO in the World Bank fast payments taxonomy ([World Bank – Fast Payments: PI‑SPI](https://fastpayments.worldbank.org/node/595)). This is direct operation rather than only regulation.

Chapter Details: The architecture, governance, functionality and uptake of government digital payment systems.  21 variables in 4 sections. Contains latest available data. Data collection by Perplexity from a variety of sources.
Definition: Whether the country has established or is actively developing an instant/real-time payment system (IPS/RTP) that enables digital payments with near-instant settlement (typically within seconds), available 24/7/365. This includes both bank-led and mobile money interoperability systems.
Comments: Benin participates in BCEAO/WAEMU regional payment infrastructures (SICA-UEMOA retail clearing + STAR-UEMOA RTGS), which the BCEAO states it operates/manages under Regulation No. 15/2002/CM/WAMU ([BCEAO – Payment Systems Management](https://www.bceao.int/en/content/payment-systems-management)). BCEAO also launched PI‑SPI (Plateforme Interopérable du Système de Paiement Instantané) for interoperable instant payments, with public launch 30 Sept 2025 and an updated list of authorized participants including several in Benin ([BCEAO press release – PI‑SPI participants at launch](https://www.bceao.int/fr/communique-presse/liste-des-participants-autorises-ouvrir-les-services-de-pi-spi-au-public-30-sept-2025);[BCEAO PDF – PI‑SPI participants as of 13 Nov 2025](https://www.bceao.int/sites/default/files/2025-11/Liste_des_participants_PI-SPI-au-13-novembre-2025.pdf)). Because PI‑SPI is launched but participant coverage is still expanding (e.g., 6 participants listed for Benin as of Nov 2025), score as partially deployed rather than fully nationwide.
